_comment: AL-Go for GitHub repository settings for the Wicket repo. SINGLE-PROJECT, MULTI-APP layout: the AL-Go project is the repository root and every app sits in its OWN subfolder - main app 'app/', companion 'actions/', tests 'test/'. NEVER put an app folder at '.': the AL compiler globs *.al recursively, so a root app folder swallows the sibling apps (an early run compiled 105 files instead of 71 and failed with AL0185 Library Assert + AL0297 50200-out-of-range). AL has no file-exclude mechanism, so separate folders are the only fix. The companion is in appFolders so a break in the posting wrappers fails the build; it depends on the main app by id and AL-Go orders app folders by dependency, so 'app' always compiles before 'actions'.
_comment_artifact: Empty => AL-Go derives the artifact from app.json's 'application' dependency (26.0.0.0), so it tracks the app target automatically and cannot drift. (The previous '//w1/24/latest' both pinned BC 24 against this BC 26 app AND had its version/country segments swapped, parsing version as 'w1'.)
_comment_version: Runtime 16.0 / BC 26 (see app.json platform/application 26.0.0.0). 'repoVersion' drives the build/version number AL-Go stamps into the apps; bump alongside app.json. RunOnWindows because BcContainerHelper/containers require Windows runners.
_comment_tests: Build the test app and run its tests in a sandbox container on every build. enableCodeCop/UICop give linting parity with the AL extension defaults; FailOn=error keeps PRs green only on clean compiles.
_comment_ranges: Declared id ranges for reference (also enforced by app.json). Main app 94100-94199, companion actions app 94200-94249, test app 94300-94349, companion tests 94350-94399 (renumbered from 50100/60100 on 2026-10-10).
_comment_template: templateUrl lets 'Update AL-Go System Files' know where to pull workflow/script updates from. Point at AL-Go-PTE (per-tenant extension template).
_comment_secrets: No secrets are required for plain CI of a w1 PTE that builds against public BC artifacts. A licenseFileUrl secret is only needed if you compile/publish AppSource apps or use objects above the standard PTE range. Deployment secrets (xxx-AuthContext) are only needed if you later add CD environments.
